final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package with labor enforcement (30/60 automatic suspension), Chapter 19 binational panels, sunset-to-review compromise (6-year term, year-5 review), 75% auto RVC with 18-month phase-in, and dairy closing Wednesday with Canada's 18%/20% tariff cuts while supply management stays intact. Friday signing locked, but dairy TRQ volumes and Congressional reopening risk remain unresolved.
minority_objections: Dairy_ag demanded full supply-management phase-out; settled for tariff cuts only after explicit TRQ volume guarantees
Canada initially refused to sign autos before seeing Chapter 19 text; yielded under bilateral-threat pressure
key_conflicts: Canada vs USTR: Chapter 19 must be in Wednesday text before auto commitment (resolved: USTR committed)
Dairy_ag vs Canada: full market access vs supply management intact (resolved: tariff cuts with quotas staying)
Multiple agents vs USTR: labor enforcement text specificity on wage-floor/union-busting triggers (resolved: explicit language committed)
Supply-chain/auto vs USTR: sunset hard-kill vs review mechanism (resolved: 6-year review, stays live unless all three kill)
key_concessions: Canada: accepted 75% RVC and labor-value floor from U.S.-Mexico bilateral, dropped demand to see enforcement text before committing to framework
USTR: committed Chapter 19 binational panels (final/binding, NAFTA-equivalent) in Wednesday text
USTR: converted sunset clause to review mechanism (6-year term, year-5 review, three-country kill vote)
Canada: tabled concrete dairy offer (18% milk, 20% cheese cuts) while keeping supply management
Dairy_ag: accepted supply management staying in exchange for tariff depth and TRQ volume expansion
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 binational dispute panels non-negotiable (stated R1, enforced through R9)
Canada: supply management stays intact (stated R8-R10, locked as baseline)
Mexico: bilateral auto/labor terms from Aug 27 untouched (stated R7-R8)
Labor_union: wage-floor and union-busting must trigger automatic suspension, not just 'labor law breaches' (stated R5-R9)
Congress: no presidential waiver on tariff suspension (stated R3, USTR committed automatic trigger)
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Congressional reopening risk after dairy closes: Mexico and supply-chain raised this R8-R10, no binding commitment secured
TRQ volume specifics: dairy_ag demanded concrete quota expansion R10, not resolved in transcript
Cost-spike risk in RVC phase-in months 12-18: auto_industry raised R10, USTR did not provide written cost-spread guarantee
Enforcement asymmetry: supply_chain_mfr asked R2 if tariff suspension hits all three countries equally, never answered
downstream_risk_variables: Dairy TRQ volumes: tariff depth locked, but actual quota expansion unspecified—could reopen market-access fight
Congressional discipline: no mechanism to prevent labor/sunset reopening if dairy slips past Wednesday
RVC compliance cost distribution: 18-month phase-in operationally feasible per auto_industry, but no written guarantee against acceleration under political pressure
Enforcement implementation: 30/60 mechanism locked in text, but inspection capacity and remediation speed untested
uncertainty_notes: Dairy TRQ volumes not finalized; Congressional reopening risk acknowledged but not contractually blocked; RVC cost-spread guarantee verbal only; enforcement mechanism text promised for Wednesday 8 AM but not yet tabled in this meeting.
